c.tagline: Fourteen islands of Scandinavian style and water.

emergency.note: 112 covers all emergencies and operators speak English; dial 1177 for non-urgent medical advice and 114 14 for non-emergency police.

english.label: Easy to get by in English

hood_landmark.Gamla Stan: The Royal Palace and medieval Stortorget square
hood_landmark.Sodermalm: Monteliusvägen clifftop viewpoint and the Fotografiska photography museum
hood_landmark.Ostermalm: Östermalms Saluhall, the historic gourmet food hall
hood_landmark.Norrmalm: Sergels torg plaza and the Kulturhuset arts centre
hood_landmark.Vasastan: Gunnar Asplund's cylindrical Stockholm Public Library

avoid.reason: Central areas very safe; gang gun/explosive violence affects certain outer suburbs (not tourist areas); pickpocketing in Gamla Stan and on the T-bana

hood_desc: Gamla Stan is Stockholm's medieval old town, a maze of cobblestone lanes and colorful facades around the Royal Palace, best for first-time visitors who want history and postcard charm though it is compact, touristy and pricey.
Sodermalm is the hip, bohemian island of vintage shops, indie cafes and buzzing nightlife, suiting younger creative travelers who want trendy streets, great views and a laid-back but lively scene.

Ostermalm is the elegant, upscale district of designer boutiques, embassies and fine dining around the historic food hall, ideal for luxury-minded visitors who value refined, quiet streets and high-end shopping.

Norrmalm is the central commercial and business core, home to the main train hub, department stores and big hotels, the most convenient base for shoppers and travelers who prize easy transport access over local character.

Vasastan is a leafy, residential area with excellent restaurants, cozy bars and a relaxed local feel, appealing to travelers who want an authentic, calmer neighborhood within easy reach of the center.

water.note: Tap water is safe and considered some of the cleanest in Europe.

transit.pay: Simplest: tap a contactless bank card or phone at the blue card readers - a single ticket (about SEK 45 / ~US$4.70) gives 75 minutes of travel on metro, buses, trams, trains and SL ferries. You can also buy tickets in the SL app, or get a reloadable SL card (SEK 20) at SL Centers and Pressbyran convenience stores. Note: you cannot buy tickets on board buses.
transit.hours: The metro runs about 5am-1am, and all night on Friday and Saturday nights; night buses cover other nights.
